start_here: Say to your AI: "Check the quotes behind my garden-tips device rows against the saved captions in captions/, then write the family file and the checked rows into out/." It reads your settings row for the piece garden-tips and runs the script on your computer, first as a check only.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope: here the settings of one batch of device rows (scope piece:<family>), as JSON: the rows, their quotes, the table columns and the wording.

values.settings: {"family": "garden-tips", "title": "Garden tips", "introduction": "Made-up rows.", "channels": {"vidA": ["BenchTalk", "Potting basics"]}, "groups": ["Care"], "rows": [{"group": "Care", "name": "say the rule, then the reason", "also": [], "what": "The viewer remembers it.", "seen": [["vidA", "water the roots, not the leaves"]], "fits": "how-to", "cost": "low", "verification": "verified"}], "columns": [{"head": "tip", "parts": [{"text": "**{name}**"}]}, {"head": "seen in", "parts": [{"text": "{seen_text}"}]}], "file_head": ["# {title}", ""], "index_marker": "<!-- {family} -->", "seen_quote": "{channel}/{video} [{stamp}] \"{quote}\"", "seen_join": "; ", "list_join": "; ", "checked_fields": ["group", "name"]}

instructions: 1. Have your settings row for this tool (see the list, or pour the two examples into your own settings list): one row per batch of device rows, id record:setting:turn-caption-quotes-into-analysis-device-rows~piece~<family>, its settings holding the rows, quotes, columns and wording.
2. Save each video's captions as json3 (yt-dlp --write-subs --write-auto-subs --sub-format json3 --skip-download), named so a glob such as captions/{video}.*json3 finds each one by video id.

3. The AI reads the tool's row with @workshop-tools tools:list {tool}, saves your settings row to a file with @own-records records:read, and runs the command in the row on your computer. Run it first without --family-file and --checked-file: it only checks every quote.

4. Read the last JSON line. rows is how many rows hold; bad names each quote that is not in its captions (or whose caption file is missing); with any bad quote the exit is 1 and nothing is written. Fix those quotes in your settings row and run again.

5. When bad is empty, run it again with --family-file out/family.md --checked-file out/checked.json (and --index-file FILE to add the family's tables to an index once). The checked rows, each with [video, second, quote], go back into your library list.

worked_examples.title: Every quote holds: the tables and the checked rows are written
worked_examples.ask: Check my garden-tips device rows against the captions and write the tables.
worked_examples.given: From tools/turn-caption-quotes-into-analysis-device-rows/test/turn-quotes-into-device-rows.test.mjs ('every quote holds'), run for real on its made-up files. Settings saved as settings.json (the garden-tips row above); captions/vidA.en.json3 has an event at 65400 ms saying "Water the roots, not the leaves". Command: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/turn-caption-quotes-into-analysis-device-rows/do-work/turn_quotes_into_device_rows.py --settings-record settings.json --captions 'captions/{video}.*json3' --family-file out/family.md --checked-file out/checked.json
worked_examples.hands_back: Last line {"result": {"rows": 1, "bad": [], "written": ["out/family.md", "out/checked.json"]}}, exit 0. out/family.md holds "# Garden tips", the group "## Care" and one table row: | **say the rule, then the reason** | BenchTalk/vidA [1:05] "water the roots, not the leaves" |. out/checked.json holds [{"group":"Care","name":"say the rule, then the reason","t":[["vidA",65,"water the roots, not the leaves"]]}].

worked_examples.title: A quote that is not in the captions writes nothing
worked_examples.ask: Check my garden-tips rows again; I changed a quote.
worked_examples.given: From the test 'a quote that is not in the captions writes nothing and exits 1', run for real: the row's quote is "water the leaves" instead, same captions, with --family-file out/nw.md.
worked_examples.hands_back: It prints BAD vidA (not in the captions) water the leaves, then the last line {"result": {"rows": 1, "bad": [{"name": "say the rule, then the reason", "video": "vidA", "quote": "water the leaves", "reason": "not in the captions"}], "written": []}}, exit 1, and out/nw.md is not created.

pour.how: Name the settings list you already keep and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example settings rows beside your own.
